sources.citation: Brown, Jason & Melissa Irvine. 2021. Avaipa, a Language of Central Bougainville. Oceanic Linguistics 60(1): 1-35. doi:10.1353/ol.2021.0000 (open-access copy, Univ. of Auckland ResearchSpace hdl 2292/55931).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The only published first-hand Simeku data: a comparative wordlist with a Simeku column (Appendix II, tables 12-13, pp. 26ff., 'transcribed from fieldnotes', fn. 7 'The Naasioi and Simeku data were also collected by the authors during the same field trip') and Table 8 'Simeku pronouns' (p. 17). No stress marks anywhere in the Simeku forms (0 occurrences of the IPA stress mark or acute accents in the appendix) and no statement on Simeku prosody; sec. 4.1 Phonology concerns Avaipa only. The one 'stress' sentence (fn. 2, p. 2) is about Naasioi: 'stress falls on the second syllable of words'. Also…

sources.citation: SIL-PNG. 2004 (data checked by Conrad Hurd, April 1992). Organised Phonology Data: Nasioi [government spelling] (Naasioi) Language [NAS], Kieta, North Solomons Province. 9 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Naasioi only (already in the catalog as naas1242): p. 2 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length): Where intonation allows it, stress occurs on the first syllable of two syllable words and the second syllable of longer words.' Its village list (p. 1) includes 'Koopei' among 18 Nasioi villages, but the data are Naasioi Proper; no Simeku/Koopei-specific remark.

sources.citation: Rausch, P. J. 1912. Die Sprache von Südost-Bougainville, Deutsche Salomonsinseln. Anthropos 7 (Nasioi 'Akzent' p. 107; Koromira section pp. 964-974) - checked for Simeku/Korpei mentions only.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Covers Nasioi and Koromira; no Simeku, Korpei or Mainoki data (a full-text search for stress/accent the whole volume scanned found none). Its Nasioi accent statement belongs to naas1242 and is not transferred here.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid sime1242 (page, JSON, langdoc) and subgroup sime1243, dialects koop1238, main1276.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic record only: Glottolog's most extensive descriptions are Ethnologue 2009 and Allen & Hurd 1965 (both 'a wordlist or less'); the sole reference at language, subgroup and dialect level is Allen & Hurd 1965 p. 18; no grammar, sketch or phonology exists for sime1242.

sources.citation: OLAC. 2025 (build 2025-11-04). OLAC resources in and about the Simeku language [smz]. www.language-archives.org/language/smz (live server could not be reached by automated download; Internet Archive copy 2026-02-16).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Catalogue only. Lists exactly one primary resource (PARADISEC AC2-NSBCVOC201, Allen & Hurd 'Languages of the Bougainville District', 1964) plus the Glottolog and Ethnologue records; no language description, phonology, text or lexicon for smz. Dialect names: Koopei, Kopei, Korpei, Mainoke, Mainoki.

sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2024. Ethnologue 27, free page 'Simeku' (via the Internet Archive 2024-09-12); Wikipedia 'Simeku language' (read online).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; vitality 6a Vigorous, South Bougainville family, <10K speakers. Wikipedia stub (3,000 speakers, 2007; dialects Mainoki, Koopei) cites Ethnologue 18 only and has no phonology section.

sources.citation: Hurd, Conrad & Phyllis Hurd. 2020 [1970]. Naasioi verbs (ed. Masayuki Onishi; revision of 'Nasioi verbs', Oceanic Linguistics 9: 37-78). SIL International, Language and Culture Archives.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Simeku stress. Notes n. 1 (after p. 42): 'There are eight dialects of Naasioi, namely: Naasioi Proper (Pirung), Oune, Pakia-Si'deronsi, Oramii, Koromira, Mainoki, Daantanai', Koopei. This paper is based on the dialect of Naasioi Proper, which the majority of the people speak.' I.e. SIL's Naasioi describers treat Simeku's two dialects (Mainoki, Koopei) as Naasioi dialects and describe Naasioi Proper (Darutue village) only.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell. 2005. The languages of Bougainville. In Anthony J. Regan & Helga M. Griffin (eds.), Bougainville before the conflict, 31-46. Canberra: Pandanus Books / ANU Press (open access). Also Regan, A. J. 2005, 'Identities among Bougainvilleans', same volume, p. 428.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress for any Bougainville language. Inventory table p. 41: Allen & Hurd list Nasioi with sub-dialect Mainoki and 'sub-language' Simeku (Korpei among dialects); p. 42: 'Simeku, Kieta District, 1,898 speakers [SIL 1980]' and 'Lantanai, Koromira, Oune and Simeku are perhaps best considered to constitute dialects of Nasioi.' Regan p. 428: the Simeku are 'regarded by linguists as speaking a sub-language of Nasioi that exhibits influence from the neighbouring Eivo language'.

sources.citation: Hamnett, Michael P. 1977. Households on the move: settlement pattern among a group of Eivo and Simeku speakers in Central Bougainville. PhD dissertation, University of Hawaii at Manoa (ScholarSpace hdl 10125/9309). 273 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnography; the only Glottolog reference naming Simeku besides the survey. p. 34: Eivo village areas differ in 'the speed with which the residents spoke, their manner of pronunciation of certain sounds and their stress patterns' (about Eivo, not Simeku); 'Informants claimed there were three kinds of Simeku: Awaipa, Kotuna, and Simeku.' Author learned some Simeku (pp. 40-41) but gives no linguistic description.

sources.note: Family-level typological survey of South Bougainville (Nasioi, Nagovisi, Motuna, Buin) with a phonology overview that may summarise Nasioi-family stress; Brown & Irvine 2021 cite it as a main overview that does not mention Avaipa, and it is unlikely to name Simeku separately.

sources.citation: Brown, Jason & Melissa Irvine. n.d. [2019-2021]. Simeku and Naasioi fieldnotes (central Bougainville field trip; source of the Simeku data in Brown & Irvine 2021, fn. 7) - and any Simeku description Jason Brown (Univ. of Auckland) publishes from them.

sources.note: The only modern first-hand Simeku phonetic corpus; Brown 2025 (Phonology 42) shows the same author works on Naasioi metrical structure, so a Simeku stress statement is most likely to come from this material. Nothing on Simeku is in the Auckland ResearchSpace as of the avai1234 search.

sources.note: The only item in any catalogue that contains Simeku (Korpei/Mainoki) wordlist data and the p. 18 subclassification comment Glottolog cites; Glottolog codes it a wordlist or less, so a stress rule is improbable, but it may carry a transcription-convention note (accent marks) and is the one document to check before calling Simeku undescribed.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur (collector); Allen, Jerry & Conrad Hurd (authors). ca 1964 [published 1965, Port Moresby: DIES, 56 pp.]. Languages of the Bougainville District. PARADISEC item AC2-NSBCVOC201, 59 page images, doi:10.4225/72/56EAC83B4627D.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Catalogue record (OAI + the Internet Archive item page) only: '58 page text.. Report on the results of the 1963 Bougainville language survey.. Contains a detailed language boundaries map'; subject languages include Simeku - smz. The page images could not be obtained: catalog.paradisec.org.au returns an automated-access block by automated download, and the Internet Archive holds only 301/302 redirects of every image URL to users/sign_in (login required). Glottolog codes it 'a wordlist or less' and cites only p. 18 'Comments on subclassification' for Simeku; a stress statement is improbable.
